A trail, not a definition

Looking for the Thread

For a while, I thought I was supposed to find the one thing that tied everything together.

I thought I needed one thing.

At UCLA Anderson, a class on personal branding made me think about this more seriously than I ever had before.

In one conversation, I asked Sasha Strauss whether all my writing needed to point in the same direction. His answer made sense: breadth can keep you in people's minds; focus can make you known for something.

Then I need to figure out my thing.

From the early exercises

Explorer

Caregiver

Curiosity

Relationships

An early attempt at putting words around it. Some felt right. Some felt like answers because the exercise needed answers.

Then I kept wandering.

I kept writing about whatever stayed with me long enough.

Data centresDogsAIFamilyClimatePeopleWorkBoredom

This did not look particularly focused.

Sometimes I was trying to understand something. Sometimes something bothered me. Sometimes it was simply a story I did not want to forget.

I also kept starting things: conversations, a podcast, small experiments, ideas that became projects and ideas that did not.

Some found an audience. Many did not.

For a while, I thought that was the problem.

I wondered whether the lack of a clear subject meant I still had not figured out what I was doing.

Was I supposed to become known for one subject—or was I simply interested in too many things?

I do not think I have a clean answer to that even now.

Now I am less sure the subject was ever the thread.

Looking back, perhaps the repetition is somewhere else.

In noticing something. Returning to it. Asking another question. Talking to someone. Changing my mind. Occasionally writing it down.

Even that may be too neat an explanation.

The website came later.

Through My Quiet Lens was not the original plan.

I needed somewhere to keep some of these things together, so I made one.

What ended up sitting beside each other

DC Decoded

Tsunami from the Sky

Celebrate 2026

PAUSE for AI

Lessons from my dogs

Participation Is Not Belonging

Not a particularly tidy collection. That may be the point.

They still do not fit perfectly.

I'm not as worried about that anymore.
